title: The nodal locus of a flat family is open and commutes with base change
statement: Let $p:Y\to T$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-pc-scheme], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], whose nonempty geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are pure of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. There is a largest open subscheme $U\subseteq Y$ such that every geometric fibre of $U\to T$ has only smooth points [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and ordinary nodes: an ordinary node over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ is a closed point with completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Formation of $U$ commutes with every base change $T'\to T$. More precisely, for every $t\in T$ and algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(t)$, the inverse image $U_\Omega\subseteq Y_\Omega$ is exactly the union of the smooth locus of $Y_\Omega$ and its ordinary nodes. In particular, $Y_t\subseteq U$ on underlying sets if and only if every singular point of $Y_\Omega$ is an ordinary node.

source.place: Tag 0DSC, lemma-locus-where-nodal: maximal nodal open and arbitrary base change, specialized to pure relative dimension one. The pointwise geometric meaning of at-worst-nodal is written out.

proof.text: Let i:Z→Y be the first-Fitting singular closed immersion. Put V equal to the fibrewise complete-intersection locus of p and W equal to the unramified locus of Z→T. The syntomic-locus theorem makes V open, and the unramified-locus theorem makes W open. Hence B=Z\(i⁻¹V∩W) is closed in Z. Since i is a closed immersion, i(B) is closed in Y. Define U=Y\i(B), a real open subset constructed without choosing any existential witness.

proof.text: The pointwise geometric criterion identifies the preimage of U on every algebraically closed-field pullback with exactly the smooth points and the closed ordinary nodes. This criterion is the only remaining local Fitting/stalk recognition input; it asserts neither openness nor maximality.

source.place: Tag 0DSC, lemma-locus-where-nodal, global construction and its geometric interpretation.

proof.text: An open immersion into a scheme locally of finite type over a field preserves closed points because the ambient scheme is Jacobson. Its stalk maps are ring isomorphisms and identify maximal ideals, hence induce equivalences of their completions. Smooth loci pull back under open immersions. Consequently the smooth-or-node predicate is invariant under open restriction. The pullback universal property identifies geometric fibres of a source open with inverse-image opens on geometric fibres, so the pointwise criterion shows that U has the required geometric fibres.

source.place: Tag 0DSC, lemma-locus-where-nodal, global construction and its geometric interpretation.

proof.text: Any source open with the required geometric fibres is contained in U on every geometric pullback, by the open-restriction comparison and the pointwise criterion. Every point y∈Y is detected on such a pullback: compose Spec of an algebraic closure of κ(y)→Spec κ(y)→Y→T and lift the first map to the pullback. Its image in Y is y. Thus the containment descends point by point and U is largest.

source.place: Tag 0DSC, lemma-locus-where-nodal, global construction and its geometric interpretation.

proof.text: For an arbitrary base change g:T′→T, associate the iterated fibre product with the geometric pullback of p at the composite geometric point. Its isomorphism is an open immersion, so the same open-immersion comparison transfers the pointwise criterion to the inverse image of U. Apply the already proved containment-and-goodness argument to obtain largestness and goodness after base change. No repeated Fitting-ideal base-change construction is needed.

source.place: Tag 0DSC, lemma-locus-where-nodal, global construction and its geometric interpretation.

proof.text: Specialize the pointwise criterion to an algebraic closure of κ(t), giving the claimed precise geometric-fibre description. The field-spectrum map Spec Ω→Spec κ(t) is surjective because the target has a single point and the source is nonempty. Surjectivity is stable under base change, so the geometric-fibre projection to the ordinary fibre is surjective. All ordinary fibre points lie in U iff all geometric fibre points do; using the criterion this is exactly that each nonsmooth point is a node.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0DSC. Construct the complement of the closed image of the bad singular part; use the sourced pointwise geometric criterion. The Lean proof then establishes open-restriction invariance, geometric-point detection, maximality, arbitrary-base-change maximality and the full-fibre assertion by pullback isomorphisms and surjectivity.
